findings.title: Early return on date override skips busy-time check, exposing already-booked slots as available
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a date override matches the slot's date and the slot falls within the override's hours, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true` and lines 133-135 immediately `return true`. This returns before the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153 runs. As a consequence, on any day where a host has a date override, all existing Cal bookings and external calendar busy times for that host are ignored during `checkIfIsAvailable`, allowing double-bookings during the date override window.

findings.title: Comparing two Dayjs instances with `===` is always false, breaking full-day unavailable date overrides
findings.body: Line 114 checks `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` to detect a 0-length date override (which represents marking the entire day as unavailable). Because each `dayjs(...).add(...)` call returns a distinct object reference, `===` between the two is always `false`. Use `.isSame(...)` (or compare timestamps) instead; otherwise a "unavailable all day" date override falls through to the range checks and slots matching the boundary or logic mistakes may not be treated as a full-day block.

findings.title: Date override range check in `checkIfIsAvailable` allows slots that partially overlap the override boundaries
findings.body: Lines 117-125 reject a slot only when `slotEndTime <= overrideStart` or `slotStartTime > overrideEnd`. This fails to reject slots that start before `overrideStart` and end after `overrideStart`, slots that start before `overrideEnd` and end after `overrideEnd`, or slots that start exactly at `overrideEnd` (`slotStartTime.isSame(overrideEnd)`). Moreover, if a user has multiple date override ranges on the same day (e.g., 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00), `.find(...)` returns `true` on the first range that does not contain the slot, causing slots in the second range to be rejected as unavailable. A slot is valid for the day's overrides only if at least one override on that day satisfies `slotStartTime >= overrideStart && slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

findings.title: Working-hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `slotStartTime` for `end` and rejects valid split schedules
findings.body: In lines 138-151, `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` instead of using `slotEndTime`, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after working hours is not caught. In addition, using `workingHours.find(...)` to return `false` when any working-hour entry for that day does not contain the slot breaks split working hours on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) and multi-day/UTC-wrapped working-hour entries: a slot in the afternoon will fail the morning entry in `.find(...)` and be marked unavailable.

findings.title: `date.start` and `date.end` in `dateOverrides` are already shifted to UTC in `getUserAvailability`, so adding `utcOffset` shifts them a second time
findings.body: `getUserAvailability` (via `getDateOverrides`) already constructs `override.start` and `override.end` as UTC `Date` instants corresponding to the organizer's local override times (for example, in the test `IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride`, 14:00 IST is stored as `08:30:00.000Z` in `dateOverrides`). In `checkIfIsAvailable`, line 107 computes `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and lines 110-123 add `utcOffset` to `dayjs(date.start)` and `dayjs(date.end)`, shifting an already-UTC timestamp by another `-utcOffset` (e.g. 08:30Z becomes 03:00Z for IST) and comparing that against `slotStartTime` (which is in UTC, 08:30Z). Similarly, in `packages/lib/slots.ts` lines 212-223, `override.start` is already in UTC, so subtracting `organizerUtcOffset` shifts the override by the organizer's offset a second time whenever `override.start` is already UTC-adjusted.
